title: History of SDIT
content: Shree Devi Institute of Technology (SDIT) was established in 2008 under the Shree Devi Education Trust, Mangaluru. The institution is located at Kenjar, Mangaluru - 574142, Karnataka. It is affiliated with Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), Belagavi, and recognized by AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education). SDIT has grown from a small technical institution into one of the prominent engineering colleges in Dakshina Kannada district. The college was founded with a vision to provide quality technical education to students from South Karnataka and beyond.

title: Vision and Mission of SDIT
content:
Vision: To be a premier technical institution of national repute by imparting quality technical education, research, and innovation that transforms students into competent professionals and responsible global citizens.

Mission:
1. To provide an excellent learning environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure.
2. To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship among students and faculty.
3. To develop industry-institute collaboration to enhance practical and professional skills.
4. To instill ethical values, leadership qualities, and social responsibility.
5. To achieve academic excellence through continuous improvement in teaching-learning processes.

title: Campus Overview and Facilities

SDIT is located at Kenjar, Mangaluru - 574142. The campus spans a well-developed area with the following major facilities:

Academic Blocks: Multiple academic blocks housing classrooms, seminar halls, and faculty rooms for each department.

Laboratories: Well-equipped labs for CSE (programming, networks, AI/ML), ECE (electronics, communication, embedded systems), ME (CAD/CAM, manufacturing), Civil (surveying, material testing), and other departments.

Library: The central library has a large collection of books, journals, and digital resources. It has reading rooms and computer access.

Hostels: Separate hostel facilities for boys and girls on or near campus.

Cafeteria: On-campus cafeteria serving breakfast, lunch, snacks, and dinner.

Sports & Gym: Cricket ground, basketball court, volleyball court, badminton court, and a gymnasium.

Medical Facility: A campus health centre for first-aid and basic medical assistance.

Administrative Block: Principal's office, HOD offices, examination section, accounts, and other administrative departments.

Auditorium: A large auditorium for college events, seminars, and cultural programmes.

title: Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
content:
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) is one of the flagship departments at SDIT. It offers a 4-year B.E. program with an intake of 60 students per year (subject to change).

Head of Department: Ms. Nisha Coutinho

The department has excellent infrastructure including:
- Programming laboratories (C, C++, Java, Python)

- AI/ML and Data Science lab

The department is affiliated with VTU and follows the VTU curriculum. Students benefit from active industry collaborations, guest lectures, workshops, and placement drives.

title: Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE)

title: Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME)

The Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME) offers a 4-year B.E. program in Mechanical Engineering. The department focuses on design, manufacturing, thermodynamics, and industrial engineering.

Laboratories include:

- CAD/CAM Lab
- Fluid Mechanics Lab
- Thermodynamics Lab
- Material Testing Lab

Students gain exposure to modern manufacturing technologies, automation, and industry 4.0 concepts. The department has strong ties with local industries and organizes industrial visits regularly.

title: Admission Procedure at SDIT
content:
Admission to SDIT's undergraduate programs follows the Karnataka state admission process:

Step 1 — Appear for KCET
Register and appear for Karnataka Common Entrance Test (KCET) conducted by Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA). KCET tests Physics, Mathematics, and Chemistry/Biology.

Step 2 — KEA Counselling
Based on your KCET rank, participate in the KEA online counselling process. Select SDIT and your preferred branch during option entry.

Step 3 — Document Verification
Carry original documents for verification:
- 10th and 12th / PUC marks cards
- KCET rank card
- Category certificate (if applicable)
- Transfer Certificate
- Migration Certificate
- Income certificate (for scholarship)
- Passport-size photographs
- Aadhar card

Step 4 — Fee Payment
Pay the admission fee at the college accounts department or through the designated online portal.

Step 5 — Management Quota
If you were not allotted a seat through KEA, limited management quota seats are available. Contact the SDIT admissions office directly for details.

For NRI / NRI-sponsored seats, separate procedures apply. Contact the admissions office.

title: Resume Writing Guide for SDIT Students
content:
A strong resume is your first impression on recruiters. Here are guidelines for creating an effective placement resume:

Resume Structure:
1. Personal Details: Name, phone, email, LinkedIn, GitHub (for CSE/ECE)
2. Career Objective: 2–3 lines specific to the role you are applying for
3. Education: Reverse chronological — B.E. (SDIT/VTU), PUC/12th, 10th
4. Skills: Programming languages, tools, technologies (only what you know well)
5. Projects: 2–3 academic or personal projects with brief descriptions and tech stack
6. Internships: If any, with company name, duration, and work description
7. Certifications: NPTEL, Coursera, AWS, etc.
8. Achievements: Academic ranks, competition wins, hackathons
9. Extra-Curricular: Club memberships, sports, volunteering

Do's:
- Keep it to 1 page (freshers)
- Use clean, professional formatting
- Quantify achievements where possible ('Improved efficiency by 30%')
- Tailor it for each job/company
- Proofread carefully

Don'ts:
- Don't add fake projects or skills
- Don't use photos unless specifically asked
- Don't add personal details like religion, caste, father's occupation (not relevant)
- Don't use colored backgrounds or fancy fonts

For personalized resume review, approach the T&P Cell or your department HOD.
source: SDIT T&P Cell + General Best Practices

title: Frequently Asked Questions — New Students
content:
Q: When does the academic year start at SDIT?
A: The academic year typically begins in August–September as per VTU and Karnataka government schedule. Exact dates are announced each year.

Q: How do I get my student ID card?
A: Student ID cards are issued within the first few weeks of admission. Contact the administrative office / examination section if yours is delayed.

Q: How do I download my hall ticket for VTU exams?
A: Hall tickets for VTU semester exams are available on the VTU website (vtu.ac.in) using your USN (University Seat Number). Your USN is given at the time of admission. The college will also inform you when hall tickets are available.

Q: What is my USN?
A: USN (University Seat Number) is your unique VTU student identification number. It is issued when your admission is confirmed by VTU. It appears on your hall ticket and mark sheets.

Q: How do I apply for leave?
A: For medical leave: Submit a medical certificate from a registered doctor to your class teacher or HOD within 3 days of returning to college. For personal leave: Submit a written application to your class teacher/HOD in advance. VTU requires a minimum of 75% attendance in each subject to be eligible for examinations.

Q: Where can I find previous year question papers?
A: Previous year VTU question papers are available on the VTU website (vtu.ac.in/qpaper) and in the SDIT library.

Q: How do I register a complaint?
A: Complaints about academics, facilities, or harassment can be submitted to: the HOD of your department, the Vice Principal's office, or the college's designated complaint redressal mechanism. Anti-ragging committee: contact immediately for ragging complaints.

title: Leave Application Procedure
content:
Students requiring leave from classes must follow the official leave procedure:

Medical Leave:
1. Inform your class teacher/HOD on the day of absence (call or message through a representative)
2. On returning, submit a medical certificate from a Registered Medical Practitioner within 3 days
3. The certificate must cover the dates of absence
4. Submit to class teacher first, then get HOD approval

Personal / Emergency Leave:
1. Submit a written application to your class teacher or HOD BEFORE the leave dates if possible
2. If it is an emergency, inform immediately and submit the application on return
3. Get approval from the HOD
4. For leave exceeding 3 days, approval from Vice Principal may be required

Attendance Rules:
- Minimum 75% attendance is mandatory in EACH subject for VTU semester exam eligibility
- Below 75% in any subject = detained from that subject's examination
- No relaxation is generally given — plan your leave carefully
- Medical leave with valid certificates can sometimes be considered by HOD for condonation (up to a certain limit as per VTU norms)

Keep copies of all leave applications and approvals for your records.

title: Hall Ticket — How to Download
content:
A Hall Ticket (Admission Ticket) is required to appear for VTU semester examinations.

How to Get Your Hall Ticket:
1. Visit VTU official website: https://vtu.ac.in
2. Go to the Examinations section → Hall Ticket download
3. Enter your USN (University Seat Number) and date of birth
4. Download and print your hall ticket
5. Get it signed by your HOD or Principal before the exam (some exam centres require this)

When is it Available?
Hall tickets are usually released 7–10 days before the examination. The college will announce when they are available.

What if My Hall Ticket is Not Available?
Possible reasons:
- Attendance shortage (below 75% in some subjects)
- Pending fee payment
- Registration error at VTU

What to Do:
1. Check your attendance with the examination section
2. Confirm fee payment with the accounts department
3. Contact SDIT examination section immediately — do not wait until exam day

Important: Without a hall ticket, you cannot appear for the VTU examination. Handle this at least 5 days before the exam.
source: VTU Examination Division + SDIT Exam Section

title: Anti-Ragging Policy at SDIT
content:
SDIT has a strict zero-tolerance policy against ragging.

Ragging is a punishable offence under UGC Anti-Ragging Regulations 2009 and Indian law.

What Constitutes Ragging:
- Any act that causes physical or psychological harm to a student
- Forcing a junior student to do any activity against their will
- Verbal abuse, intimidation, or humiliation
- Any form of eve-teasing or harassment

What to Do if You Face Ragging:
1. Report immediately to the Anti-Ragging Committee (available at the college)
2. Contact the SDIT helpdesk: +91 9353619812
3. Call the national Anti-Ragging Helpline: 1800-180-5522 (toll free)
4. File a complaint online at: antiragging.in

Punishment for Ragging:
- Suspension or expulsion from the institution
- FIR filed with police
- Criminal proceedings as per law

All complaints are treated confidentially. Do not hesitate to report.
